docs.title: Description
docs.text:
modular-slam is a flexible, high-performance library for building and experimenting with Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) systems in both Python and C++. It’s designed to make SLAM prototyping fast and enjoyable: you can mix and match components - data acquisition blocks, optimization backends, data association strategies, and more—without fighting a large, monolithic codebase.

Use modular-slam when you want to: - Prototype quickly – swap components in and out with minimal boilerplate. - Explore new ideas – compare different models, solvers, or data-association strategies side by side. - Scale to real systems – go from small experiments to real-world SLAM deployments without rewriting everything. - Evaluate and benchmark – compare SLAM performance against other popular systems with ease.

In short: experiment freely, iterate quickly, and keep full control over your SLAM pipeline.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Modular architecture Compose SLAM pipelines from interchangeable pieces: localization, mapping, optimization, sensor fusion, and more.

  • Multi-language Use Python for rapid prototyping and C++ for performance-critical components, without maintaining two completely separate codebases.

  • Prebuilt Components Common SLAM building blocks such as visual odometry, IMU fusion, and graph-based optimization are provided out of the box.

  • Extensible by design Plug in your own sensors, cost functions, or backends via a clean extension / plugin system.

  • Cross-platform Target Linux, macOS, and Windows with a single codebase.

  • Real-time oriented Built around efficient data structures and parallel execution to support real-time SLAM workloads.
